pharm: Bispecific delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3)-directed CD3 T-cell engager for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer

summary: Tarlatamab (Imdelltra) is a DLL3 x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) granted accelerated approval in 2024 for adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) with disease progression on or after platinum chemotherapy. It binds DLL3 on tumor cells and CD3 on T cells to drive T-cell-mediated tumor killing. Dosing uses step-up infusions of 1 mg on Day 1 and 10 mg on Day 8, then 10 mg IV every 2 weeks; at that dose the objective response rate was 40% with a median duration of response of 9.7 months. It carries a boxed warning for cytokine release syndrome (CRS), including life-threatening or fatal reactions, and neurologic toxicity including ICANS, with mandatory 22- to 24-hour monitoring after each step-up dose. Additional risks include cytopenias, serious infections, hepatotoxicity, hypersensitivity, and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Treatment of adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) with disease progression on or after platinum chemotherapy

moa: Tarlatamab is a bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) that binds delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), a protein expressed on the surface of most small cell lung cancer cells with limited normal-tissue expression, and CD3 on T cells. By linking T cells to DLL3-expressing tumor cells, it activates T cells and triggers release of cytotoxic mediators that kill the tumor cells. Step-up dosing is used to reduce the incidence and severity of cytokine release syndrome during initial T-cell activation.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to tarlatamab or any excipient
relative: Active serious infection (initiate only after infection is controlled)
History of significant neurologic disease (may complicate ICANS assessment)
monitor: Live vaccines during treatment (immunosuppression and cytopenias)

preg: Based on its mechanism of T-cell activation, tarlatamab can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment.
lact: There are no data on the presence of tarlatamab in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is established for renal impairment. Monitor closely during CRS episodes with hypotension, which can reduce renal perfusion, and adjust supportive care as needed.
hepatic: No established dose adjustment; hepatotoxicity is reported, so monitor liver function tests and withhold or discontinue for significant transaminase or bilirubin elevation per labeling.

Live vaccines (risk of vaccine-related infection during immunosuppression; avoid)
moderate: Hepatotoxic drugs (additive liver injury risk; monitor liver function tests)
Sedating or neurotoxic drugs around step-up dosing (may confound ICANS assessment; monitor neurologic status)
minor: No clinically significant CYP-mediated interactions are expected for this antibody therapy
interactions.food: Not applicable (IV administration); maintain adequate hydration.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; avoid excess alcohol during CRS-risk periods and cytopenias.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC with differential and liver function tests; monitor neurologic status and CRS signs as clinically indicated.

counsel: CRS and neurologic toxicity including ICANS can be life-threatening; seek emergency care for fever, trouble breathing, confusion, trouble speaking, severe sleepiness, seizures, or loss of consciousness
You will be closely monitored for 22 to 24 hours after each of the first two step-up doses and must stay within 1 hour of the hospital for 48 hours after each
Report signs of infection at once (fever, chills, cough); low blood counts are common and you will have frequent blood tests
Tell your team about liver symptoms (yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, right-sided abdominal pain) and all other medicines and vaccines
Use effective contraception during treatment and tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan pregnancy, or are breastfeeding

At the end of the IV infusion
Prolonged, consistent with a bispecific T-cell engager protein; supports every-2-week maintenance dosing
Pharmacodynamic effect persists between doses with 10 mg every-2-week maintenance
Refrigerate per labeling; do not freeze; protect from light; use reconstituted and diluted solutions within labeled time limits
pearls: Boxed warning: CRS including fatal reactions and neurologic toxicity including ICANS; first BiTE T-cell engager approved for ES-SCLC
Mandatory 22- to 24-hour monitoring after Cycle 1 Day 1 (1 mg) and Day 8 (10 mg), plus 48-hour proximity to care after each step-up dose
Maintenance is 10 mg IV every 2 weeks, with a 40% response rate and 9.7-month median duration of response at that dose
Step-up dosing is essential to reduce CRS incidence and severity; withhold or permanently discontinue per labeling for CRS or ICANS
Monitor blood counts, liver function, and infection throughout therapy; embryo-fetal toxicity requires contraception
missed: Tarlatamab is given on a supervised infusion schedule, so there is no patient-managed missed dose. If an infusion visit is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule; do not attempt to make up doses independently, as step-up and timing rules affect CRS risk.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for tarlatamab overdose. Exaggerated CRS, neurologic toxicity, cytopenias, or infection may occur. Withhold treatment and provide intensive supportive care with monitoring for CRS, neurologic status, blood counts, liver function, and infection. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
